text:
maya: Heads up — seeing nvme avg-latency spike in ap-southeast1, GPU attach queue growing. Affected nodes gnode-aps1-23/24/29. Anyone oncall? iostat shows crazy small writes.

sre-bot: ALERT: nvme-latency > 20ms on gnode-aps1-23,gnoj-aps1-24 (threshold 10ms) — automated alert triggered 02:34 UTC

leo: I'm jumping on it. I'll cordon gnode-aps1-23 and reprovision, but we should check janitor scrubs. Maya which cron ran?

maya: scrub job ran 02:15; saw spike in smallwrite rate. snippet:
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1       0.12  12345.8   8.2M  1.9M   154.0  35.6  22.1  0.02  22.1  0.45 93.4
```

alex: probable write amplification from janitor overlap + thermal throttle on hotstripe. Quick mitigation: reduce janitor concurrency in region to 1 and throttle smallwrites. e.g.
`kubectl set env deployment/janitor CONCURRENCY=1 -n infra-ap-southeast1`

jin: doing the scale now — scaling down janitor replicas to 1 in ap-southeast1. Will post results in 2 mins :thumbsup:

ops-bot: action: scaled deployment/janitor to 1 replica in infra-ap-southeast1 by jin at 02:40 UTC

leo: after scale down, avg-latency dropped to ~6ms on affected nodes, GPU attach backlog cleared. Strong candidate root cause. Recommend follow-up: add rate limit to janitor, add thermal-aware gating, and a canary scrub schedule.

maya: filed INC-2026 and created storage ticket STOR-88 'hotstripe janitor concurrency safeguard'. Assigning to storage-team. Moving to ops postmortem later. Thanks all.
